theme: कर्म का बंधन नहीं, अकर्ता भाव; गुण और कर्म के आधार पर व्यवस्था, पर भगवान अछूते हैं / Action without ego; order through guṇa and karma, yet the Lord remains untouched by action.
context: Krishna has just taught that divine action is for the protection of the good and the restoration of dharma. Now he explains that the fourfold social order arises from guṇa and karma, but the Lord Himself is not bound by actions or their fruits.
contextHindi: कृष्ण ने अभी यह समझाया है कि दिव्यता का कार्य धरम की रक्षा और अधर्म के नाश के लिए होता है। अब वे बताते हैं कि चारों प्रकार की व्यवस्था गुण और कर्म के आधार पर बनती है, लेकिन भगवान स्वयं कर्मों और उनके फलों से बंधे नहीं हैं।
sanskritDevanagari:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः |
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ||४-१३||
transliteration:
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ .
tasya kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam ||4-13||

wordByWord.meaning: the fourfold order or varṇa; not merely a label but a social and functional differentiation within human life.
according to the division of guṇa (qualities) and karma (actions); the phrase points to a cosmic and ethical ordering, not arbitrary rank.
the non-doer; Krishna is being described as free from the egoic sense of agency.
imperishable, unchanging, not consumed by action or time.

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक बहुत शांत, लेकिन गहरा सत्य कहता है। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि चारों वर्ण—ब्राह्मण, क्षत्रिय, वैश्य, शूद्र—गुण और कर्म के अलग-अलग विभाजन के अनुसार अस्तित्व में आते हैं। इसमें यह नहीं कहा गया है कि कोई मनुष्य अपने स्वभाव से ऊपर-नीचे है; बल्कि यह कहा गया है कि मानव जीवन की भूमिकाएँ प्रकृति के गुणों और व्यक्ति के कार्यों के आधार पर अलग-अलग हो सकती हैं। फिर कृष्ण कहते हैं: ‘तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्धि’—उसके कर्ता के रूप में भी मुझे जानो। यानी मैं कर्म का कारण हूँ, लेकिन मैं स्वयं कर्म का अहंकारी कर्ता नहीं हूँ। मैं अकर्ता हूँ, अव्यय हूँ। इसी को समझकर मनुष्य कर्म करता है, पर बंधन नहीं बनाता। यही है योग का सार: कामना से मुक्त होकर, अहंकार से रहित होकर, कर्म करना।
clearEnglish: This verse is not a statement that social divisions are permanent or morally absolute in themselves. The point is that human roles and capacities arise from guṇa and karma, which are part of the order of nature. Krishna does not deny that social and functional differentiation exists; he places it within a larger cosmic frame. The crucial claim is that the Lord is the source of the order, yet not trapped in it as an egoistic doer. The word akartāraṃ is important: it means not that God is inactive, but that divine action is not driven by personal attachment, desire, or self-claiming. This is a profound contrast with ordinary human action, which often becomes binding because the ego says, “I did this.” In the spiritual life, the aim is to act without claiming agency over the result. That is not irresponsibility; it is freedom from the binding loop of doership and reward.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states that the fourfold order is created by the Lord according to guṇa and karma, and that the Lord is not an egoic doer. It is a statement about cosmic order and divine freedom from action.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: Traditional commentaries often explain guṇa and karma as the basis of varied natural tendencies and duties, while stressing that the Lord remains untouched by the results of actions. This is a doctrinal interpretation, not a literal claim that every social arrangement is a final metaphysical truth in itself.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A reasonable practical inference is that we should judge actions by their effects, intentions, and responsibility, not by egoic ownership. We can honor roles and duties without making the self the center of the action.

practicalApplication.label: Role without ego
practicalApplication.text: When you do a job, study, serve, or care for family, notice whether you are acting from responsibility or from the need to be seen and rewarded. Shift from “I am the doer” to “I am participating in a larger flow.”

reflectionQuestion: When a responsibility is assigned to you, how much of your stress comes from egoic ownership rather than from the duty itself?
reflectionQuestionHindi: जब कोई जिम्मेदारी आपके सामने आती है, तो आपके तनाव का कितना हिस्सा “मैं ही इसका कर्ता हूँ” की भावना से आता है, और कितना काम की जिम्मेदारी से?
